Price damage is minimal while options traders pay up for near term protection. Trust the VIX Spike Detector for the next few sessions, because options reprice before prices break, and size for a vol expansion even though the Crash Index is quiet.
⚠ These two disagree: Divergence composite zone CALM, **32.6%** of **43** pairs diverging vs Mother jaws score **100**
The broad count of diverging pairs is modest, but the six strongest pairs all score **80** with large correlation flips. Trust the jaws score for risk, since relationships that flip together matter more than a headcount of mild drifts.

AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The market is quiet on the surface and uneasy underneath. The Crash Index reads 1 out of 10, but the VIX Spike Detector sits at tier 2 of 4 with a 60% probability, and both skew and backwardation are active. Options traders are paying for protection that price action has not yet earned.

The macro model reads CONTRACTION at 70% confidence, while the contrarian score of 77 says capitulation conditions are in place. Those two readings point in different directions, and that is the central tension. A weak growth backdrop with washed out sentiment rewards patient buyers, but only after the vol curve calms down. The Nasdaq 100 is down 4.6% in five days while the Dow is up 1.7%, so leadership is rotating away from growth. Keep new risk small until backwardation clears, and favor the parts of the market that are holding up over the ones that are breaking.

The main risk is a vol expansion that starts before the Crash Index reacts. Six major pairs, including SMH against SPY (+0.89 to -0.05) and KRE against XLF (+0.43 to -0.59), have flipped their correlations, so hedges built on old relationships may not hold. The stance flips constructive if VIX backwardation fades and the VIX tier drops to 1. It turns defensive if the Crash Index climbs above 2 while the Nasdaq 100 keeps lagging.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means two assets that normally move together are starting to move apart. Correlation drift is the size of that change, comparing how tightly they moved over the past year with how they move now.

The composite zone is CALM, with 32.6% of 43 pairs diverging, 8 bearish and 6 bullish, for a net bias of +2. That headline is mild.

The jaws picture is not mild: the mother jaws score is 100, and six pairs score 80 at DEEP DIVERG. SMH against SPY went from +0.89 to -0.05, so chips no longer drive the index.

SPY against TLT went from +0.76 to -0.15, which changes how bonds hedge stocks. KRE against XLF went from +0.43 to -0.59, so regional banks split from the wider financial sector.

T10Y2Y moved from -0.51 to +0.29, MOVE from +0.31 to -0.37, and ETH against BTC from -0.66 to +0.43. Old relationships are breaking.

Review hedges that depend on them.

HYG weakness would be the most important, since credit stress is what turns a vol scare into a real drawdown.

Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Leadership is split and the spread is wide. In Asia, the Hang Seng leads at +7.5% over five days while the Kospi lags at -7.3%, a 14.8 point gap inside one region.

Europe is steadier, with the CAC 40 at +3.7% and the FTSE at +1.3%. In the US, the Dow leads at +1.7% and the Nasdaq 100 trails at -4.6%.

In crypto, ETH leads at +8.3% and SOL lags at +0.1%. The Kospi weakness lines up with the break in the SMH to SPY link, so chips look like the pressure point.

For the US session, expect growth and tech to stay heavy and the Dow and defensives to hold better. A Nasdaq 100 bounce that closes the gap with the Dow would ease the vol warning.

Continued Kospi weakness would add to it.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 1/10 · WATCH — 1-2 signals, monitoring
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The Crash Index and the VIX Spike Detector measure different things, so their gap is a coherent state. The Crash Index at 1 out of 10 reads realized damage: prices, breadth, credit.

Little has broken there. The VIX Spike Detector at tier 2 of 4 with a 60% probability reads what options traders expect next.

Skew is active, meaning puts cost more than calls, and backwardation is active, meaning near term vol costs more than later vol. That combination says buyers want protection now.

The adaptive trigger is off, so the signal is not yet at its most urgent. All three vol to equity confluences (HYG, small caps, yen) are inactive, so no stress has spread into credit or funding.

The practical read is a market that is calm but braced. Trust the options market for timing risk over the next sessions and the Crash Index for confirmation that damage has started.

A move in the Crash Index from 1 to 3 would turn the options warning into a confirmed one.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 1/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

Aggregation of all panel signals across the 4 cross-asset buckets. RISK-ON = risk appetite (cyclical, equity, EM). RISK-OFF = flight to defensives (TLT, gold, JPY). Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
